research_questions.A-LAYER: How do collective memory theories explain intergenerational cultural transmission, and what mechanisms cause language/writing loss across generations?
research_questions.BOZ-01: What geographic and economic factors enabled horse domestication in the Eurasian steppe around 3500 BCE, and how did this affect trade networks?
research_questions.KURG: What do kurgan burials reveal about Scythian social hierarchy, and to what extent does the Gimbutas kurgan hypothesis explain Proto-Indo-European origins?
research_questions.KÜR-ARAZ: How did the Shulaveri-Shomu culture function as a Caucasus culture bridge, and what genetic/ceramic evidence exists for 4000-2000 BCE diaspora?

claims.text: Halbwachs' theory establishes that collective memory functions only within social group frameworks, with different groups maintaining distinct historical narratives

confidence_history.reason: Multiple academic sources confirm Halbwachs' foundational framework

claims.text: Assmann distinguishes between communicative memory (80-100 year span, informal) and cultural memory (institutionalized, ritual-based transmission)
claims.notes: Central distinction in cultural memory studies

claims.text: Intergenerational transmission breakdown (parents raising children in dominant language) is the critical tipping point for language extinction
claims.notes: Key mechanism of language loss identified in endangered alphabets research

claims.text: Horse domestication occurred at Botai culture, northern Kazakhstan, around 3500 BCE based on metrical analysis of horse remains

confidence_history.reason: Multiple independent archaeological studies confirm 3500 BCE Botai domestication

claims.notes: Supported by Nature publication and multiple academic sources

claims.text: Botai culture evidence includes three independent types: metrical analysis of metacarpals, pathological bridling marks, and mare's milk residues in pottery

confidence_history.reason: Direct chemical and pathological evidence documented

claims.notes: Multi-modal evidence from organic residue analysis (delta13C/deltaD values)

claims.text: Western Eurasian steppe (lower Volga-Don region) served as the homeland of modern domestic horses that spread globally from ~2000 BCE

confidence_history.reason: Nature article documents global expansion pattern

claims.notes: Genetic analysis confirms replacement of local populations

claims.text: Pazyryk kurgans preserved extraordinary textiles and mummies through permafrost ice formation, dating to 6th-3rd centuries BCE

confidence_history.reason: Direct archaeological evidence from Ukok Plateau excavations

claims.notes: Penn Museum documentation and UNESCO heritage listing

claims.text: Issyk kurgan contained over 4,000 gold ornaments with animal motifs, indicating elite Scythian-Saka status around 5th century BCE
claims.notes: Also known as 'Golden Man' discovery near Alma-Ata, Kazakhstan

claims.text: Gimbutas' kurgan hypothesis (1956) links kurgan archaeology with linguistics to locate Proto-Indo-European origins in Pontic-Caspian steppe

confidence_history.reason: Widely cited but subject to ongoing archaeological and genetic debate

claims.notes: Alternative genetic hypotheses exist (steppe migration models contested)

claims.text: Recent ancient DNA analysis shows Scythian elites inherited high social status and formed hereditary dynasties, with family ties across 60+ mile distances

confidence_history.reason: Max Planck genetic study and multiple media sources confirm findings

claims.notes: 2026 study reveals nearly 50% of elite burials were female

claims.text: Scythian kurgan burials reveal social hierarchy through grave goods disparity: elite graves contain gold/weapons/imported vessels, common graves simple or empty
claims.notes: Pattern consistent across Eurasian steppe Iron Age sites

claims.text: Shulaveri-Shomu culture occupied South Caucasus from ~6000-4000 BCE across Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia, and northern Iran

confidence_history.reason: Multiple archaeological surveys confirm geographic range

claims.notes: Type sites include Shulaveri, Shomutepe, and Mentesh Tepe

claims.text: Mentesh Tepe Neolithic population resulted from admixture between Anatolian farmer-related and Caucasus/Iranian populations

confidence_history.reason: Genome-wide analysis published in Communications Biology

claims.notes: Demonstrates that agricultural adoption involved population admixture

claims.text: Shulaveri-Shomu culture produced earliest evidence of domesticated grapes and winemaking (~6000 BCE) at Gadachrili Gora

confidence_history.reason: Chemical analysis of pottery residues confirmed

claims.notes: Earliest evidence in the Near East, significant for understanding Neolithic subsistence

claims.text: In 5th millennium BCE, gene flow from Mentesh Tepe-related groups mixed with Pontic Steppe populations contributing to Late Bronze Age Caucasian makeup

confidence_history.reason: Genetic evidence supports migration and admixture patterns

claims.text: Shulaveri-Shomu ceramics feature incised and relief decoration influenced by Near Eastern traditions (Hassuna, Halaf), with anthropomorphic female figurines indicating ritual significance

confidence_history.reason: Ceramic typology established but symbolic interpretation requires further analysis

claims.notes: Limited detailed symbolic analysis available in current literature

evidence.description: Halbwachs' theoretical framework shows collective memory is group-specific and socially constructed
evidence.notes: Foundational text in memory studies

evidence.description: ResearchGate publication confirms Halbwachs as founding text for contemporary memory studies
evidence.notes: Peer-reviewed verification of Halbwachs' foundational status

evidence.description: Assmann's distinction between communicative (80-100 year, informal) and cultural memory (institutionalized, ritual) framework
evidence.notes: Core theoretical distinction in cultural memory studies

evidence.description: Endangered Alphabets Project documents intergenerational transmission breakdown as critical tipping point for language extinction
evidence.notes: Practical documentation of language loss mechanisms

evidence.description: Archaeological metrical analysis of Botai horse metacarpals shows similarity to Bronze Age domestic horses rather than Paleolithic wild horses
evidence.object_provenance: Botai culture archaeological excavations, Kazakhstan, 3700-3100 BCE radiocarbon dated
evidence.notes: Metrical analysis is standard zooarchaeological evidence

evidence.description: Pathological bone markers on Botai horses indicate bridling and possible riding
evidence.notes: Pathological markers indicative of tack pressure

evidence.description: Organic residue analysis using delta13C and deltaD values of fatty acids in Botai pottery confirms mare's milk processing
evidence.object_provenance: Botai pottery ceramic vessels with internal lipid residues
evidence.notes: Chemical isotope analysis is direct biomarker evidence

evidence.description: Bridling marks on Botai horse skeletons indicate developed harness technology
evidence.notes: Pathological evidence supports hypothesis of secondary products exploitation

evidence.description: Mare's milk production identified through pottery chemical analysis indicates secondary products economy
evidence.object_provenance: Botai ceramic vessels with preserved lipid residues
evidence.notes: Koumiss production still practiced in Kazakhstan, confirming traditional practice depth

evidence.description: Nature article documents genetic evidence that modern domestic horses originated in lower Volga-Don region and spread globally by 2000 BCE
evidence.notes: Genetic analysis shows replacement pattern across Eurasia

evidence.description: Pazyryk kurgans preserve textiles, mummies, and wooden artifacts through permafrost ice formation creating barrow congelation conditions
evidence.object_provenance: Ukok Plateau, Altai Mountains, Siberia, 6th-3rd centuries BCE
evidence.notes: Exceptional preservation due to unique hydrogeological conditions

evidence.description: Penn Museum documentation and UNESCO heritage listing confirm Pazyryk textile preservation and cultural significance
evidence.notes: Institutional archival documentation

evidence.description: Issyk kurgan excavation (1969) documented over 4,000 gold ornaments with animal motifs in single burial
evidence.object_provenance: Issyk kurgan, 31 miles east of Alma-Ata, Kazakhstan, 5th century BCE
evidence.notes: 'Golden Man' discovery is one of richest single burials in Iron Age Eurasia

evidence.description: Gimbutas' kurgan hypothesis integrates kurgan archaeology with Proto-Indo-European linguistics
evidence.notes: Influential but contested theoretical framework

evidence.description: Alternative genetic studies propose competing models of Proto-Indo-European expansion beyond kurgan hypothesis
evidence.notes: Genetic archaeology has challenged pure kurgan hypothesis since 2000s

evidence.description: Max Planck genetic study reveals Scythian elite hereditary status through familial DNA links across multiple burial sites
evidence.object_provenance: Scythian kurgan burials across Eurasian steppe, genetic analysis (2026)
evidence.notes: Ancient DNA evidence definitively demonstrates hereditary power transmission

evidence.description: Archaeological excavation reports document disparities in grave goods between elite and non-elite Scythian kurgans
evidence.notes: Consistent pattern across Eurasian steppe Iron Age societies

evidence.description: Multiple archaeological surveys establish Shulaveri-Shomu geographic range across South Caucasus
evidence.object_provenance: Archaeological site surveys in Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia, Iran, 6000-4000 BCE
evidence.notes: Type sites include Shulaveri (Georgia), Shomutepe (Azerbaijan), Mentesh Tepe (Georgia)

evidence.description: Genome-wide analysis of Mentesh Tepe collective grave documents admixture between Anatolian farmer and local Caucasus/Iranian populations
evidence.object_provenance: Mentesh Tepe archaeological cemetery, ancient DNA sampling and sequencing
evidence.notes: Published in Communications Biology, peer-reviewed genetic evidence

evidence.description: Chemical residue analysis of pottery from Gadachrili Gora identifies wine production markers dating to ~6000 BCE
evidence.object_provenance: Gadachrili Gora pottery vessels with wine residue biomarkers
evidence.notes: Earliest evidence of winemaking in Near East, revolutionary for understanding Neolithic subsistence

evidence.description: Genetic evidence shows gene flow from Mentesh Tepe-related groups into Pontic Steppe populations during 5th millennium BCE
evidence.notes: Demonstrates documented diaspora pattern through ancient DNA

evidence.description: Archaeological ceramic analysis shows Shulaveri-Shomu pottery features incised/relief decoration influenced by Hassuna-Halaf traditions with anthropomorphic female figurines
evidence.notes: Symbolic interpretation of figurines requires further contextual analysis
